messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Threat
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Threat
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Memory → Triggers
  - Threat → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Arjun, a 29-year-old painter from a South Asian background, found himself ensnared in a web of anxiety and fear following a traumatic mugging last year. The incident had left an indelible mark on him. He vividly recalled the evening when he was walking home from a late job, paintbrushes still tucked under his arm, when a group of men confronted him. The memory of that confrontation loomed heavily in his mind, making every shadow and every unfamiliar figure on the street feel like an imminent threat, as if danger could strike again at any moment. He remembered the rush of adrenaline, the fear coursing through his veins as they demanded his wallet and phone. The ordeal lasted mere minutes, but it felt like an eternity, and he would wake up in a cold sweat, haunted by nightmares of the event—dreams where he relived the moment again and again, the panic rising in his chest as he struggled to break free. Each time he awoke, he felt a surge of irritability, an angry outburst bubbling just beneath the surface. It was as if he had become a stranger to himself, his body always on high alert, constantly scanning his surroundings for potential threats. 

The physical locations where the mugging had occurred became charged with anxiety. The memories flooding back in those places carried a palpable sense of danger, as if the threat he had once faced was still lurking just out of sight, making each return feel like an invitation to experience fear anew. Simply passing by those streets triggered a rush of intrusive memories, causing his heart to race and his palms to sweat. These memories flooded back with such intensity that they felt alive, forcing him to relive the fear and vulnerability of the event as if it were happening anew, amplifying his sense of threat. These moments magnified the tense state his body had adopted; he felt as if he were perpetually ready to react to danger, a sensation that transformed his daily life into a battleground. The memories that surfaced in those moments only served to heighten his sense of danger, making him feel as though he was back in the confrontation, every detail sharp and close, reinforcing his belief that he was under constant threat. The world outside was a constant reminder of his trauma, and each spatial trigger intensified his belief that he could no longer trust the people around him. Each time he encountered these triggers, his body would react with a surge of fear, amplifying the sense of threat that loomed over him, as if danger was not just a memory but a present reality. He had come to mistrust everyone, convinced that anyone could become a threat, and this growing isolation made him feel more detached from those he loved. This deep-seated belief that he was always vulnerable led him to interpret every interaction with others as a potential source of danger, making him more anxious and guarded in social situations. His negative beliefs about his own safety shaped how he viewed the world, instilling a persistent sense of danger that made him hyper-aware of any situation where he might feel exposed or vulnerable. Having come to believe that he was always at risk, Arjun approached even the most mundane interactions with an underlying tension, bracing himself for potential threats that existed only in his mind. 

As he grappled with these feelings, Arjun found it difficult to piece together the memory of the mugging. Yet, whenever those fragmented memories surfaced, they were accompanied by a crushing sense of immediacy, leading him to feel as if the danger of that night was still very much alive, echoing within him. He often felt as though he was only recalling fragments of the experience, the gaps gnawing at him and fueling his guilt. Each time those fragments emerged, he couldn't help but think they revealed a deep flaw within himself, reinforcing his belief that he was weak and unworthy of safety, which further fueled his anxiety about future threats. Once those memories broke through, they amplified his sense of danger, as if the past were still alive within him, creating an ever-present anxiety that made it hard to feel secure anywhere. Each time those fragments surfaced, they deepened his conviction that he had failed to protect himself, reinforcing his belief that he was inadequate and leaving him feeling hopeless and trapped. He would sit in his studio, attempting to deliberate on the event, but the harder he tried to access the painful recollections, the more elusive they became. This incomplete picture of the traumatic event compounded his feelings of guilt; he often questioned why he hadn’t fought back or run faster, which only deepened his sense of inadequacy. The memories, though fragmented, remained potent triggers—each recall would send him spiraling back into that moment of vulnerability, enhancing his sense of danger and leading him to believe that he was incapable of relying on anyone, not even himself.

Arjun's negative appraisals shaped his perception of the world, creating a vicious cycle. His mistrust of people steered him towards isolation, which only fortified his belief that he couldn’t rely on others. As he withdrew from social interactions, he would find himself alone in his thoughts, the memories of the mugging replaying in his mind, reinforcing his feelings of vulnerability. The threat he felt was not just from the memories themselves; it seeped into every aspect of his life, making even casual encounters feel like potential ambushes, further pushing him into isolation. This constant reflection contributed to his irritability and made him more sensitive to perceived slights from others, aggravating his readiness to react defensively. With an ever-present sense of threat, even minor interactions felt charged; he interpreted casual remarks as veiled attacks, convinced that others were judging him, and this only solidified his desire to withdraw further into isolation. His memories of the traumatic event seemed to taunt him, leading him to interpret innocent interactions as threats, convinced that others were judging him or harboring malicious intent. Each day became a struggle as he navigated through the layers of his trauma, caught in an ever-tightening loop of anxiety and avoidance.

When Arjun finally sought help, he felt a glimmer of hope mixed with the fear of confronting his trauma. He was acutely aware that the memories he carried would not only resurface but could also amplify his fears, making every session feel like stepping into a minefield of emotions he had long tried to avoid. He harbored a deep-seated worry that delving into his memories would only serve to amplify his feelings of guilt and mistrust, but he knew he could not continue living in this state of hypervigilance. He longed to reclaim the joy he once found in painting, to reconnect with his wife and friends without the shadow of his trauma looming overhead. Yet, he feared that engaging with those memories would only serve to reinforce his belief that he was permanently broken, trapped in a cycle of pain and mistrust that he couldn't escape. With each session, he hoped to find a way to unravel the knots of his experience, to understand the connection between the past and present, and to ultimately heal from the scars that had come to define his daily existence.

violation_explanations: The vignette does not explicitly convey how triggers influence negative appraisals.
The vignette does not demonstrate how negative appraisals lead to a sense of threat.
The vignette lacks a clear connection indicating how memory affects negative appraisals.
The vignette does not show how perceived threat influences encounters with triggers.
